impls.interpretation_choices:
I checked the plan's sha256 before the run: 8c7bf923...782f19a. Every choice below is also listed in summary.md section 2.

Candidate weeks:
- Panels A and B use bars that open before 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC. B's 1 h files run to 2026-10-12, so I cut them there.
- A and B candidate weeks are the Mondays from 2020-05-04 to 2026-09-28. The partial trailing week 2026-09-28 fails the 99 % rule and is counted as skipped.
- Panel C runs from 2025-01-13 to the week of the last bar, 2026-10-19. That week is partial, so it is skipped and counted.
- The 99 % rule means at least 1996 of 2016 5 m bars, or at least 167 of 168 1 h bars, in both the week and the prior week.

Levels and touches:
- O is the open of the Monday 00:00 bar.
- P1 levels are generated only when D > 0. D = 0 happened in 1 coin-week on A (LTC 2022-10-24), 5 on B and 3 on C on the high side, and 0 / 1 / 2 on the low side. The real level is still scored in those weeks.
- P2 window is [ws-252h, ws-84h). "Broken" means a later bar's high is above P2H (no tolerance). The 10 bps rule is |P2/PWH-1| >= 0.001.
- I added one rule the plan does not state: the P2 window must hold at least 99 % of its bars. This removed 1 coin-week on A and 8 on B.
- A touch is the first bar of the week with high > L x 1.00005 (or low < L x 0.99995).

Returns and patterns:
- Returns are simple, signed bps. Net is gross minus 9.43 for F and minus 14.62 for B and S.
- F: entry_time is the touch-bar open. The exit is the close of the bar ending at touch open + h, so on 1 h panels the 1 h exit is the touch bar's own close.
- 1 h closes start with the 1 h bar that contains the touch.
- B: confirmation is a close strictly beyond L, and the confirming bar must open inside week w.
- S: "inside" is close <= L, the complement of "beyond", so the first 1 h close after the touch decides S. The 4 h limit therefore never binds. Closes exactly equal to L occurred on 10 / 116 / 2 S entries (panels A / B / C).

Reel rates (panel A):
- reject60 looks at the 12 five-minute closes from the touch bar, with r = 10 bps on both sides; if neither threshold is reached it counts as not rejected.
- "continued" looks at the 288 five-minute bars after the confirming close. A bar that both continues and returns to L is counted as not continued. These ties are 347 of 2422 real events: counting ties as continued gives 86.8 %, excluding them gives 84.6 %, against 72.5 % reported.
- Reel rates in results.json pool both sides and all P1 multiples.

Bootstrap and statistics:
- The weeks are the sorted distinct used week starts. Each panel gets one matrix default_rng(11).integers(0, W, size=(2000, W)), shared by every test in that panel.
- p_one_sided is the share of draws with diff <= 0. real_net_p is the share with real net mean <= 0. CIs are the 2.5 / 97.5 percentiles.
- Halves are split by week start before or after 2023-07-01, and halves.n counts real events. Halves are null on C.
- coins_pos_diff is literally real minus P1, including on the P2 rows; the real-minus-P2 count is in diagnostics.json. A coin with no events in a cell counts as not positive.
- Daily Sharpe uses net bps booked on the UTC date of the exit-bar end, zero-filled calendar days from the first used week, std with ddof=1, times sqrt(365).

Checks:
- tests_synthetic.py: 38 hand-computed checks, 0 failures.
- crosscheck.py (pandas): used weeks, PWH/PWL, touch flags and the PWH F 4 h mean all match, BAD 0.
- worked.py / worked_1h.py: three panel A events and four Delta 1 h trades re-derived from the raw data all MATCH.
- The vectorised bootstrap equals an explicit resampling loop.

Runtime: A 12.8 s, B 21.6 s, C 2.7 s; crosscheck 18.5 s.

impls.interpretation_choices:
I checked the plan hash before and after (8c7bf923...f19a, unchanged). Where the plan was ambiguous I took the most literal reading; the full list of 19 choices is in summary.md section 2.

(1) Candidate weeks are Mondays whose whole week lies inside the window. For A and B that is 2020-05-04..2026-09-21, so the week starting 2026-09-28 is neither used nor counted as skipped. For C it is 2025-01-13..2026-10-12 (full weeks only). A and B bars are cut off at open < 2026-10-01; C is not cut off.

(2) Coverage rule: at least 99% of the expected bars (1996 of 2016 at 5 m; 167 of 168 at 1 h) in both week w and week w-1. Skipped coin-weeks: A 11 (all DOGE), B 117, C 0.

(3) O = open of the first bar of week w. The plan says O always lies inside [PWL, PWH], but it does not: D_H<=0 / D_L<=0 occurs A 1/0, B 5/1, C 3/2 times. In those cases I kept the real level and created no P1 levels on that side.

(4) P2 window = bars opening in [W-252h, W-84h). "Unbroken" means max high from the window end to W is <= P2H (and min low >= P2L for P2L). "Differs by 10 bps" means |P2/PWx - 1| >= 0.001. The P2 window has no coverage requirement; it is below 99% coverage in A 1 and B 8 used coin-weeks.

(5) Touch = first bar opening in week w with high > L(1+0.5e-4) (or low < L(1-0.5e-4)). t0 = that bar's open time.

(6) Returns are simple returns on the entry price in bps, signed by direction. F enters at L. Net = gross - 9.43 for F and - 14.62 for B and S.

(7) F exits at the close of the bar whose close time is exactly t0+h. On 1 h panels the 1 h exit is the touch bar's own close. F entry_time in the events file = t0. No exits were dropped on any panel.

(8) On A, the 1 h closes are the closes of the HH:55 5 m bars. "At or after the touch" means close time >= t0 + bar length, which starts with the close of the hour containing the touch bar.

(9) B confirms on the first 1 h close strictly beyond L whose hourly bar opens inside week w. There is no other time limit.

(10) S scans the 1 h closes with close time in [t0+bar, t0+4h]. It stops at the first close strictly beyond L and enters at the first close strictly inside L. A close exactly equal to L counts as neither and the scan continues (A 10, B 121, C 2 equal closes). In practice S fires exactly when the first 1 h close after the touch is inside L, so the 4 h clause is almost redundant. S is not restricted to week w.

(11) reject60 uses the closes of the 12 5 m bars opening in [t0, t0+60min), touch bar included, with r = 10 bps. Sides are pooled; per-side rates are in extras.json.

(12) "continued" uses the 5 m bars in [tc, tc+24h). If one bar reaches both C(1+r) and L, the order is unknown and I count it as NOT continued. This choice matters: real 0.7246 as reported, 0.8679 if ties count as continued, 0.8458 if ties are excluded (347 ties out of 2422 confirmations).

(13) Pooled P1 = all four multiples and both sides, weighted by event.

(14) Bootstrap: the units are the distinct used week starts (334 for A and B, 92 for C). One index matrix per panel, default_rng(11).integers(0, n_weeks, (2000, n_weeks)), is shared by all tests. Each draw's mean is the ratio of summed event totals to summed event counts. The CI is the 2.5/97.5 percentiles; p = share of draws with diff <= 0. I checked the vectorised version against a plain loop: they agree to 4e-14.

(15) Halves are split by week start: H1 is weeks starting before 2023-07-01.

(16) coins_pos_diff is real minus P1 on every row, including the P2 rows, as the contract literally says. The count against each row's own control is in extras.json.

(17) Daily Sharpe uses net bps summed by UTC exit date, with zero on days without exits. The calendar runs from the first candidate Monday to the last candidate Monday + 8 days. Annualised with sqrt(365), ddof 1.

(18) Panel B's nine coins use hourly/*.csv as given. XRP and LTC have 2022 holes there, so 5 of their coin-weeks are skipped.

disagreements.what: D1: S (sweep-and-reclaim) events when the first 1 h close after the touch is exactly equal to L. These are the only event-level differences. Panel A has 10 such level-events: 5 are in X only and 5 enter 1 h later in Y. Panel B has 116: 54 in X only, and 62 enter later in Y (59 by 1 h, 2 by 2 h, 1 by 3 h). Panel C has 2, both in X only. All are PWH/PWL or P2 levels; P1 levels never tie. All F and B rows, all P1 rows, all level prices and all touch and reel numbers match to float noise. At the primary horizon S 4 h, X to final: A real n 1316 to 1311, gross -15.41 to -15.48, diff vs P1 -10.63 to -10.70, P 0.9315 to 0.9325. B diff -13.10 to -12.50. C real net -40.50 to -40.41. 254 results.json numbers are outside tolerance because of D1, plus 7 on the S Sharpe rows (D1 and D3 together).
disagreements.cause: X engine.py level_events, S loop: if side*(cpx-L) > 0 it breaks, otherwise it enters. So a close equal to L counts as inside, and X enters at L. Y engine.py level_events, S loop: beyond breaks, strictly inside enters, and equal is counted as neither (n_equal) and the scan continues. Checked by hand from the raw 5 m CSVs. ADA 2022-08-08 PWH 0.538: the 06:00 close is 0.538, then the next three closes are all beyond L, so X has an S event and Y has none. DOGE 2022-03-14 PWH 0.12444: the 15:00 close is 0.12444 and the 16:00 close is 0.12419, so X enters at 15:00 and Y at 16:00.
disagreements.resolution: Adopt Y. Both readings are defensible, and Y's is the more literal. The plan marks non-strict relations explicitly ('at least r inside L', '>= 99 %', '>= 10 bps', '>= 6 of 9'). Every relation it spells out without such a marker is strict (high > L(1+0.5bp), D_H > 0, and 'beyond L', which both implementations read as strict). Its own step 'O always inside [PWL, PWH], so D_H > 0' also treats 'inside' as strict. A close exactly at L is therefore neither 'back inside L' nor 'beyond L'. X's partition (inside = not beyond) is reasonable, but the plan text does not state it. The final results use Y's rule, and final/test_s_ties.py (4 cases, all pass) checks it.

disagreements.what: D2: coin_weeks_skipped. A: X 20, Y 11. B: X 142, Y 117. C: X 9, Y 0. The gap is exactly one coin-week per coin. Used weeks (2995 / 8233 / 828), events, means and tests are identical.
disagreements.cause: X run.py makes candidate weeks run to WIN_END_EXCL-1 (A, B) or G.end-G.dt (C). So the partial trailing week (2026-09-28 for A and B, 2026-10-19 for C) is a candidate, and it fails the 99 % coverage rule. Y run.py only takes weeks that lie wholly inside the window: last week 2026-09-21 for A and B, last full week 2026-10-12 for C.
disagreements.resolution: Adopt Y. Panel C says 'full weeks only' outright. For A and B, the window is 2020-05-01..2026-09-30, so the week starting 2026-09-28 is not a coin-week of the panel. The 99 % rule is about missing bars, not about where the window is cut. Only the reported count changes. Not a disagreement, but flagged: both implementations count 11 DOGE pre-listing weeks as skipped, and on panel A those are all 11 of the skips.

disagreements.what: D3: daily_sharpe, all 9 values on every panel; on S, D1 also contributes. The largest gap on F and B is 0.0107 (C F 1h), and the largest on S is 0.025 (B S 1h). The plan uses this only as information; it is not a gate.

Y's calendar is fixed by the study window plus the longest possible hold (a B entry at the last hourly close of the week, held 24 h). X's calendar ends wherever the last real exit happened to fall, so it depends on the outcomes.

disagreements.what: D4: no number differs. X adds a rule that the P2 window must have at least 99 % of its bars; Y has no such rule. The rule touches 1 A coin-week (DOGE 2020-07-20) and 8 B coin-weeks (DOGE 2020-07-20; XRP, LTC, IOTA, TRX, VET, XLM, ZEC 2022-04-11).

disagreements.resolution: Adopt Y, with no P2-window coverage rule, because the plan's P2 definition has no coverage condition. It changes no event and no number; the X_patched rerun confirms this.
